Low-accuracy value. Check against NIST ASD: the two rated decay branches of this level (458.4 nm, A = 1.3e6, and 788.96 nm, A = 3.5e7 s^-1, accuracy C / C+) sum to 3.63e7 s^-1, so 41 ns x sum(A_NIST) = 1.49 (1/sum(A_NIST) would be 27.5 ns): this lifetime and the NIST rates are mutually inconsistent, see 'conflicts'. Not shown on the page: lifetime x sum(A_NIST) = 1.49, inconsistent with the NIST rates (accuracy C+/C); second-hand value, moved to alternatives 2026-10-02

not_found: 882 nm cooling line: isotope shifts for the nine stable isotopes and the 131Xe (and 129Xe) hyperfine constants of 6p[5/2]3 measured in a MOT by Walhout, Megens, Witte, Rolston (Phys. Rev. A 48, R879 (1993)) - still closed (Semantic Scholar: closed access; no arXiv, NIST or repository copy; 2 web searches; the open papers citing it - Vassen review, Bounds et al. 2023, Doery et al. 1998 - do not reprint its table). Husson, Grandin, Kucal (J. Physique 40, 551 (1979)) was opened in this pass and does NOT cover 6p[5/2]3 (it covers 6p'[1/2]1, 6p'[3/2]1, 7p[3/2]1, 6p'[3/2]2, 6p[3/2]2, 4f[3/2]1, 5f[3/2]1, all stored now).

823 nm line isotope shifts (D'Amico et al. 1999): abstract only, no numbers; the 841.15 and 820.86 nm shifts of Bounds et al. are recorded instead. Third pass: Phys. Rev. A 60, 4409 (1999) still closed (no open copy found); its hyperfine constants remain second-hand from Bounds et al.
Absolute optical frequencies of 882 / 823 nm better than NIST: not located.
Directly measured lifetime of 6p[5/2]3 and A values newer than NIST: 33.03 ns is the Vassen-review table value.
Experimental reduced matrix elements: none located.

Lifetime of 129Xe / 131Xe 3P2 (hyperfine-quenched): the Walhout abstract states it is much shorter in 129Xe but gives no number. The 6s'[1/2]0 clock-state decay rate is now stored from the Opt. Lett. abstract.

Level-resolved radiative lifetimes of the 6p, 6p', 7p, 6d levels: Inoue, Ku, Setser (J. Chem. Phys. 81, 5760 (1984)) abstract gives only ranges (30-48 ns for 6p and 6p', 68-172 ns for 7p); Bruce et al. (J. Chem. Phys. 92, 2917 (1990)) and Boewering et al. (84, 715 (1986)) abstracts carry no numbers; full texts are paywalled. Suzuki & Shimoda (J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 43, 1977; OSTI abstract) give 35 +- 2 ns and 37 +- 4 ns for levels written '6p22' and '6p01' and 520 +- 30 ns for '5d33'; the notation could not be mapped to NIST levels with certainty, so they were not stored. Third pass (2026-10-02): all three J. Chem. Phys. papers are closed access per Semantic Scholar and no repository copy or reprinted table was found (2 web searches); only single second-hand numbers could be stored: 34 ns for 6p[5/2]3 (Horiguchi et al. 1981 via Doery et al. 1998) and 41 ns for 6p'[1/2]0 (thruster-plume measurement via Eichhorn et al. 2022). Das & Karmakar, Eur. Phys. J. D 32, 285 (2005) (lifetimes of nf and 8s, 9s levels) - OSTI abstract carries no numbers.
Interferometric 6s[3/2]2-6s'[1/2]0 clock frequency (Opt. Lett. 20, 1421 (1995)): not opened. Third pass: Semantic Scholar lists Opt. Lett. 20, 1421 (1995) as closed; no NIST-hosted copy found.
AFIT thesis 'Investigation of Metastable Xenon' (129Xe hyperfine coefficient of 6p[5/2]3 at 882 nm) blocked for automated access.
conflicts: 131Xe B(6s[3/2]2): D'Amico et al. 255.7(0.6) MHz vs Bounds et al. 246.7(2) MHz (823 nm) and 259(7) MHz (841 nm); A(131) 705.4(0.4) vs 708.3(1) MHz. The D'Amico values, consistent with the atomic-beam intervals of Faust & McDermott (|A129| = 2384.50 MHz derived), are used.
129Xe A(6s'[1/2]1): D'Amico -5808(2) MHz vs Bounds -5782(4) / -5785(2) MHz (about 25 MHz apart).
3P2 lifetime 42.9(9) s (Walhout 1994) is less than half of the theoretical values (96-150 s); no competing measurement.

6s'[1/2]0 lifetime: measured spontaneous rate 7.8(38) s^-1 (0.128 s, 49 % uncertainty) vs theory 0.078 s (12.8 s^-1), 1.3 sigma apart; the effective room-temperature lifetime is 13.3 ms because of blackbody-induced deexcitation.
8s[3/2]1 energy: Ramsey-comb value for 132Xe 90932.44142 cm^-1 vs NIST 90932.432 cm^-1 (natural mixture), 0.009 cm^-1 apart.

Brandi et al. 2001 calibrated energies (136Xe 8d[1/2]1 94228.0187, 8d[3/2]1 94685.4822; 132Xe 7s'[1/2]1 95800.5867 cm^-1) lie 0.003-0.015 cm^-1 above the NIST values; the measurement is older than 20 years, so NIST stays in use.

Hyperfine constants from the 1979 level-crossing work of Husson et al. (now stored as alternatives) vs the laser-spectroscopy values kept as main entries: 129Xe A(6p'[1/2]1) 1981.3(1.5) vs 1977(1) MHz; A(6p'[3/2]1) -4427.0(1.5) vs -4424(1); A(6p'[3/2]2) -2885.2(3.6) vs -2894.6(4.7); A(6p[3/2]2) -886.5(0.9) vs -889.6(0.4); 131Xe B(6p'[3/2]2) -17.1(0.3) vs -14(17) and 3.5(1.0) MHz; B(6p[3/2]2) 30.3(0.6) vs 23.8(0.4) MHz. The level-crossing A values depend on the g_J used.
6p[5/2]3 lifetime: 33.03 ns (Vassen review, equal to 1/A_NIST) vs 34 ns (Horiguchi et al. 1981 as quoted by Doery et al. 1998); no uncertainties printed.

6p'[1/2]0 (89860.015 cm^-1) lifetime: the second-hand thruster-plume value 41 ns (Eichhorn et al. 2022, no uncertainty) exceeds 1/sum(A_NIST) = 27.5 ns (A = 3.5e7 + 1.3e6 s^-1, NIST accuracy C+ / C); lifetime x sum(A_NIST) = 1.49. Either the NIST rates are too large or the plume lifetime is too long; the 41 ns value is kept as the only level-specific number found but should be treated as low accuracy (verification pass 2026-10-02).
notes: Hyperfine entries taken from the comparison table of Bounds et al. are second-hand (method 'compilation', original named in the source); Bounds' own results are listed as alternatives. Isotope-shift keys are kept exactly as printed (pair label 'A-B' with a negative value); see each note on the unverified sign convention. Values converted from mK carry the printed mK numbers alongside. Level energies are NIST ASD values from data/xe/levels.csv; Paschen names in the labels. Entries marked '(abstract)' were read on the publisher's abstract page or HAL record only. Added 2026-10-01 (second pass): VUV isotope shifts of Brandi et al. are printed as nu(136) - nu(A) (positive = lighter isotope at lower frequency); Dreissen et al. print nu(A) - nu(132). 'use_source' / 'use_url' name the paper a use annotation was taken from. Added 2026-10-02 (third pass, papers opened in full): Husson, Grandin, Kucal 1979 (hyperfine constants, printed in mK, converted with 1 mK = 29.9792458 MHz, printed numbers kept in A_mK / B_mK) and Huet et al. 1979 (Lande factors; identical to the NIST ASD values, now with uncertainties). The 4f[3/2]1 and 5f[3/2]1 levels were added for their hyperfine constants only.
